newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Budget panel sets weaker rouble assumption in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Budget panel sets weaker rouble assumption in 1997.

text.p: The conciliation commission of government and parliamentary representatives working on the 1997 draft budget decided to base the budget on an average rouble rate in 1997 of 5,750 per dollar, the commission said on Friday.
The government's draft being discussed by the panel had assumed a rouble rate of 5,560 per dollar.

Under the sloping rouble corridor, a sort of crawling peg providing for a gradual devaluation of the rouble, which expires at the end of this year, the rouble is due to be in a 5,500-6,100 range on December 31.
The rouble was 5,453 per dollar on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX) on Friday.
The commission agreed to base the budget on an annual inflation rate in 1997 of 11.8 percent, compared with two scenarios of 11.5 or 11.8 percent proposed by the government.
This would work out at 0.93 percent a month on average.
The panel agreed on a forecast of gross domestic product of 2,727 trillion roubles, implying real GDP growth of about two percent in 1997.
